messages:
maria: quick heads-up — ran a full autotune sweep for quant kernels across sm86/sm90 for seq=32/512/2048. results look noisy but there’s a clear perf regression on INT8 matmul for sm86 at seq=2048 (tokens/s down ~18% vs previous pick)
aj: can you paste the perf numbers and the kernel candidates you tried?
maria: sure. summary first: int8_fused_v2 (default pick) vs int8_alt_v1 vs fp16_reference. sm86 @ seq2048: int8_fused_v2 = 820 tok/s, int8_alt_v1 = 980 tok/s, fp16_reference = 1050 tok/s. previous autotune had been picking int8_alt_v1 for long sequences; new selector picked fused_v2 after last commit.
simon: hmm that suggests our perf model weights for "long_seq" shifted. did the commit change the workspace or tile heuristic?
maria: looks like it. profiling snippet (top kernel times for fused_v2 on sm86 seq2048):
```
# perf top-like dump (summary)
matmul_fused_v2: 42.1%
softmax_attn: 18.4%
kv_update: 9.9%
load/store overhead: 6.3%
other: 23.3%
```
aj: do you have a flamegraph or kernel launch params? maybe fused_v2 has lower occupancy for long seq on sm86 (register/SM pressure)
maria: launch params show grid=..., block=..., workspace= ~1.2GB. int8_alt_v1 uses a tiling that reduces workspace and increases occupancy. flamegraph points to matmul_fused_v2 spending more time in atomic reductions vs alt.
liz: also check KV cache behavior — long seq causes lots of KV reads. if the fused kernel assumes contiguous KV strides it might be suffering cache misses on sm86 memory subsystem. sm90's L2/mesh improvements could hide that (explains why sm90 didn't regress).
aj: good call. can we reproduce locally with a minimal harness? CI perf job flagged the regression on main, commit abc123. ci-bot: perf-alert: PR #2345 (commit abc123) — p99 latency regression +15% on sm86-2048-int8 autotune test. see /ci/perf/1772
simon: tentative mitigation: change kernel-selector scoring: add a per-arch fallback weight for sm86 when seq >= 1024 to bias toward int8_alt_v1 or fp16_reference. also add a quick check: if workspace > 1GB on sm86 prefer alt.
maria: prototype config I tested:
```json
{
  "arch_overrides": {
    "sm86": {
      "long_seq_threshold": 1024,
      "workspace_limit_bytes": 1073741824,
      "preferred_kernels": ["int8_alt_v1","fp16_reference"]
    },
    "sm90": {}
  }
}
```
aj: that looks reasonable. we should also add an autotune metric that records KV read bandwidth and memory stalls so scoring can learn this pattern rather than heuristics.
liz: agree. for short-term: roll selector change behind a canary for sm86 dedicated pool and run sweep again. if p99 improves, promote.
maria: one more note: int4 paths show even more variance across arches; for int4 we may want to lock picks per-model shape instead of dynamic selection until autotune gets more samples.
simon: opened a tiny PR with the scoring tweak and canary flag: https://git.redwood/infra/PR-512 (wip). maria — can you attach the harness script & perf traces to the PR?
maria: will do, uploading delta now. also adding a small regression test: run autotune for seq=2048 on sm86 using the exact batch distribution we saw in production.
aj: thanks. after canary run, if stable, update the per-arch default signatures in model-catalog so dedicated/private deployments pick the correct kernel.
ci-bot: note: scheduled nightly sweep will pick up new PR fixtures; disable sweep if you want manual runs.
liz: tagging @eng-sre for canary rollout coordination. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks — will post results in this thread after the canary (ETA ~2h).
